# Parroquia San Juan de la Cruz

> Catholic Carmelite parish in Nuevo Cuscatlán, La Libertad, El Salvador, cared for by the Discalced Carmelite friars. A house of prayer, encounter, celebration and community.

## What this parish is
Parroquia San Juan de la Cruz is a Roman Catholic parish in Nuevo Cuscatlán, La Libertad, El Salvador, served by the friars of the Order of Discalced Carmelites (Carmelitas Descalzos). It is not a diocesan parish: it carries the specific charism of the Discalced Carmel, which within the Catholic Church is contemplation and the spiritual life. The parish began as a Carmelite retreat house project, was established as a parish after the foundation stone was laid around 2005, and recently marked fifteen years since its founding. It sits next to the Casa de Retiro El Carmelo and has parking inside the grounds.

- Opens every day at 6:00 a.m., together with the Blessed Sacrament Chapel

- Saturday: closes after the evening Mass
- Sunday: closes at 8:30 p.m.

## Offerings (confirmed)
- Baptism: $50.00
- Confirmation at the Cathedral of San Salvador: $8.00 per person
- Wedding and other celebrations: set by the parish office; the wedding offering is non-refundable

## What the parish offers
- Holy Mass and confession
- Personal spiritual direction with a Carmelite friar, arranged through the parish office
- Baptisms, first communion, confirmation, marriage and adult Christian initiation
- Marriage preparation, including a one day intensive retreat run by the Matrimonios en Victoria movement, with a certificate accepted by other parishes
- Thanksgiving Masses for anniversaries, fifteenth birthdays, schools and institutions
- More than twenty active groups: liturgical ministries, youth communities by age, catechesis, social outreach, movements and service teams
- Use of the church by people and institutions from outside the parish, with an offering

## Questions people ask
- What time is Mass? Sunday 7, 9 and 11 a.m., 5 and 7 p.m.; weekdays 7 a.m. and 6 p.m., with an extra 11 a.m. Mass on Thursday; Saturday 7 a.m., noon and 6 p.m.
- What time does the church open? Every day at 6:00 a.m.
- Can I get married or have a child baptised here even if I am not a parishioner? Yes, through the parish office.
- How do I ask for spiritual direction? Call the parish office; the secretary books an appointment with a friar.
- How do I join a group? Through the group's own leader or through the parish office.
- Fray, father or priest? All three are correct. Most Carmelite friars are also ordained priests.

## Who the parish serves
Families and individuals in Nuevo Cuscatlán and the surrounding residential areas of La Libertad, El Salvador, plus people from elsewhere in the country who want to celebrate a sacrament in this church, and institutions such as schools and companies booking a Mass.

## Carmelite context
The Order of Discalced Carmelites was founded in sixteenth century Spain by Saint Teresa of Ávila with Saint John of the Cross. Missionaries reached Latin America in the same century through Mexico. Central America was founded by two Spanish provinces: Navarre (Guatemala and Panama) and Aragón-Valencia (El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica). The Carmelites arrived in El Salvador in the 1960s, beginning at Hospital Rosales, and founded their first parish in the country, El Carmen in Colonia Roma. Key feast days: San Juan de la Cruz on 14 December (patronal feast), Virgen del Carmen on 16 July, Santa Teresa de Jesús on 15 October, Santa Teresita del Niño Jesús on 1 October.
